Moves a box (lined up with the world unless it is given a turn) from one point to another through the bodies of a physics world and returns the first body that it touches. It is a ray with a size, which is what a program needs for its own ground checks, wall sliding, camera collision and projectiles. All points are in the world. It sees bodies where their entities are now, but not legacy colliders or the meshes of `LinePick`.

What was hit is kept for `GetPhysicsHitEntity`, `GetPhysicsHitX`, `GetPhysicsHitY`, `GetPhysicsHitZ`, `GetPhysicsHitNX`, `GetPhysicsHitNY`, `GetPhysicsHitNZ` and `GetPhysicsHitDistance` until the next ray, shape or point query. The point is where the shape touched, the normal points out of the body and the distance is how far the centre of the shape went. A shape that starts inside a body hits it at distance 0.

```blitzbasic
body = PhysicsBoxCast(0, 1, 0, 10, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
If body Then Print "Wall after " + GetPhysicsHitDistance()
```
@param x1 Where the shape starts, x. This is the centre of the shape.
@param y1 Where the shape starts, y.
@param z1 Where the shape starts, z.
@param x2 Where the shape ends, x. Bodies beyond this are not hit.
@param y2 Where the shape ends, y.
@param z2 Where the shape ends, z.
@param half_x The half size of the box along x.
@param half_y The half size of the box along y.
@param half_z The half size of the box along z.
@param pitch The turn of the box around x, in degrees, as `TurnEntity` takes them. 0 (default) is not turned.
@param yaw The turn around y, in degrees. 0 (default) is not turned.
@param roll The turn around z, in degrees. 0 (default) is not turned.
@param mask_low The layers to look at, as bits 0 to 31 of a mask (bit n is layer n). -1 (default) looks at all layers.
@param mask_high The layers 32 to 63, as bits 0 to 31 of a mask. -1 (default) looks at all layers.
@param sensors 1 also finds sensors (see `PhysicsSensor`); 0 (default) leaves them out.
@param world The physics world, 0 (default) for the default world.
@returns The entity of the body that was hit, or 0 if there is none.
@gap The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
